text: (excited) In July 1518, a woman named Frau Troffea started dancing in a Strasbourg street.
(surprised) And she didn't stop? Just kept going?
(excited) She didn't stop for days, and within a week, dozens had joined her.
(surprised) Dozens? Did they all just start dancing too?
(excited) By late summer, hundreds were dancing through the city, and many collapsed.
(excited) Some died of heart attacks, strokes, or exhaustion. Officials hired musicians and built a dance hall.
(surprised) A dance hall? What did they think that would do?
(excited) They hoped the crowd could dance the curse out of its system. It didn't work.
(excited) Historians still argue. Ergot poisoning, mass hysteria, and stress are all on the table.
(excited) So a whole city lost control of its own bodies, and nobody could explain why. Comment "PLAGUE" and I'll send you the link.
